2.1.3 BINOMIAL NOMENCLATURE

There are millions of plants and animals in the world. The plants and animals in our area are known by their local names. The same plants and animals are known by different common names in different languages, even within a country. This creates the confusion on recognizing the organisms. So, the standard method of naming the organisms is required. Carolous Linnaeus develops a system of scientific or technical names for animals and plants. The system is known as binomial nomenclature. In this system, each organism is given a name of two words. The first word indicates the genus or generic epithet. The second word refers to the species or specific epithet. For example: the scientific name of rice is written as Oryza sativa. In this binomial name, Oryza represents the genus and sativa indicate a particular species. These binomial nomenclatures ensure that a name has not been used for any other organism.

The binomial nomenclature (scientific name) are established on basis of certain principles and criteria developed by number of scientists belonging to International Code for Botanical Nomenclature (ICBN), International Code for Zoological Nomenclature (ICZN), International Code for Bacterial Nomenclature (ICBaN) and International Code of Viral Nomenclature (ICVN).

Some important rules of binomial nomenclature are as follows: 1. The Scientific name should be derived from Latin or Greek languages or should be Latinized. 2. The scientific name consists of two names, in which the first name denotes the generic name while second name denotes the specific name. 3. The generic name should always begin with capital letter while specific name should begin from small letter. 4. The scientific name should be written in italics if printed or computerized or should be separately underlined if handwritten. 5. The generic name is always single word and can be abbreviated by using only its first letter followed by dot if the generic name is mentioned earlier (like, E. coli) while specific name may be single or compound and never be used in abbreviated form. (like, Hibiscus rosa-sinesis) 6. The name of author is written either in full or in abbreviated form after the name of species. E.g. Mangifera indica L. Here ‘L’ indicates the name of author i.e. Linnaeus.
